title: Electrotaxis Studies of Lung Cancer Cells using a Multichannel Dual-electric-field Microfluidic Chip
protocol: Design an individual acrylic layer pattern using commercial software such as AutoCAD.
Review the design of the four-layer acrylic sheet pattern and confirm inter-layer connections.
Fabricate all acrylic sheets and double-sided tape by laser ablation using a CO2 laser scriber.
Turn on the laser scriber and connect it to the controlling laptop.
Run commercial software and open the designed pattern file.
Place an acrylic sheet or double-sided tape on the X-Y-Z stage of the laser scriber.
Set the focus of the laser beam on the surface of the acrylic sheet or double-sided tape using an auto-alignment stick.
Send the designed pattern to the laser scriber for machining.
Remove protective paper from the acrylic sheets using forceps.
Blow the surface clean with nitrogen gas after removing the protective paper.
Stack the acrylic sheets and bond them together under a pressure of 2 kg/cm² in a thermal bonder at 110 °C for 45 min.
Prepare the microscope cover glass as the cell culture substrate in the chip.
Put the cover glass into a staining jar.
Fill the jar with a ten-fold dilution of the detergent listed in the material list.
Put the cover glass and staining jar in an ultrasonic steri-cleaner.
Clean the cover glass for 15 min.
Pour out the diluted detergent from the staining jar.
Refill the jar with distilled water.
Repeat step 1.5.2 three times.
Dry the cleaned cover glass by blowing it with nitrogen gas.
Adhere the dried cover glass to the flow/electrical stimulation channel assembly using double-sided tape.
Adhere 13 pieces of acrylic adaptors to the individual openings in Layer 1 of the MDF chip assembly with super glue.
Sterilize the complete MDF chip assembly with UV irradiation for 30 min.
Sterilize all plastic tubes, finger-tight nuts, and microcentrifuge tubes by autoclaving at 121 °C for 15 min.
Connect fluoroplastic tubes to the medium inlet and outlet adaptors of the MDF chip assembly via 3-way stopcocks.
Take 2.5 ml of CO2-equilibrated PBS using a 3 ml syringe.
Connect the syringe with PBS to the 3-way stopcock of the inlet plastic tube.
Connect an empty 3 ml syringe to the 3-way stopcock of the outlet plastic tube.
Incubate PBS in a 37°C 5%-CO2 cell culture incubator overnight to obtain CO2-equilibrated PBS.
Seal the openings of the blue and green adaptors on the Layer 1 PMMA sheet with white solid finger-tight nuts.
Fill the salt bridge channels and culture chambers with CO2-equilibrated PBS using a syringe.
Put the CO2-equilibrated PBS-containing MDF chip in the 37°C 5%-CO2 cell culture incubator overnight for O/N incubation.
Flush away bubbles in the channels by a rapid PBS flow using two syringes if necessary.
Drain the PBS in the channels via the 3-way stopcock connected to the medium outlet tube.
Take 2.5 ml of CO2-equilibrated Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM).
Replace the syringe connected to the inlet with a new one containing DMEM.
Refill the channels with the medium.
Temporarily remove solid nuts on the green adaptors.
Inject 3% hot (>70°C) agarose into the salt bridge channel through the opening in the green adaptors.
Prepare hot agarose by dissolving 1.5 g of agarose powder in 50 ml of PBS.
Sterilize the agarose solution by setting a holding time of 20 min at 121°C in the autoclave.
Stop injecting the agarose when the liquid fills three-quarters of the length of the salt bridge channel.
Screw solid nuts onto green adaptors after agarose injection.
Replace solid nuts on blue adaptors with translucent tubular finger-tight nuts.
Load 3% pre-heated agarose into tubular nuts.
Embed Ag/AgCl electrodes into tubular nuts before agarose solidification.
Inject CL1-5 lung cancer cells into the culture chambers, one chamber at a time.
Culture CL1-5 lung cancer cells in complete medium in a 75T cell culture flask at 37 °C in a 5% CO2 atmosphere.
Sub-culture cells every 3 to 4 days.
Use cells for electrotaxis experiments that are less than 25 passages from the original source.
Add 2 ml of 0.25% trypsin buffer to exponentially growing CL1-5 cells.
Incubate for 2 min in a 37 °C, 5%-CO2 cell culture incubator for cell detachment.
Terminate the detachment process with 6 ml of 10% FBS DMEM.
Centrifuge the cells at 300 g for 5 min at room temperature.
Discard the medium and suspend the cell pellet with 5 ml of PBS.
Count the number of cells in the PBS.
Take 1 x 10^6 cells and centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min at room temperature.
Discard the PBS.
Suspend the cells with pre-warmed CO2-equilibrated DMEM.
Adjust the cell density to be 1 × 10^6 cells/ml.
Incubate the complete medium in the 37 °C, 5%-CO2 cell culture incubator overnight to obtain the CO2-equilibrated DMEM.
Set up for electrotactic experiment from the outlet of the MDF chip.
Inject 0.3 ml, 1 × 10^6/ml, of the cells into the chip.
Incubate the cell-seeded MDF chip in the cell culture incubator (set at 37 °C and 5% CO2) for 2-4 hr.
Install the MDF microfluidic system onto a transparent indium tin oxide glass (ITO) heater.
Measure the temperature of the MDF chip with a K-type thermocouple clipped between the MDF chip and the ITO glass.
Control the ITO heater with a proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller.
Set the MDF microfluidic system incubation temperature to 37 °C with the PID controller.
Mount the temperature-controlled MDF chip assembly on the computer-controlled X-Y-Z motorized stage of an inverted microscope.
Pump complete medium into the culture chambers through the inlets with a four-channel syringe pump at a flow rate of 20 μl/hr.
Incubate the cells for another 16-18 hr at 37 °C in the MDF chip.
Prepare a 10 mM stock solution of Rho-associated protein kinase inhibitor Y27632 by dissolving 10.6 mg in 3 ml sterile water.
Dilute the 10 mM stock solution to 50, 25, and 5 µM using 10% FBS DMEM medium.
Pump medium containing 50, 25, 5, and 0 μM kinase inhibitor into each culture chamber at a flow rate of 20 μl/min for 10 min.
Incubate the cells in the kinase inhibitor for another 60 min at 37 °C.
Set the medium flow rate to 20 μl/hr.
Connect electrical wires from a DC power supply to the MDF chip via the Ag/AgCl electrodes on the chip.
Serially connect an ammeter in the electric circuit.
Monitor the electric current in the MDF chip using the ammeter.
Turn on the DC power supply and set the ammeter current to 86.94 μA by adjusting the power supply voltage between 15 and 19 V.
Control the motorized stage using a MATLAB GUI program.
Move the MDF microfluidic system to the observation regions using the motorized stage.
Record cell images using a digital single-lens reflex (SLR) camera mounted on the microscope.
Take microscopic images using a 4X objective lens at intervals of 15 min for 2 hr.
Run NIH ImageJ 1.47 V.
Analyze the distance from the initial to the final positions of the cell's centroid.
Import nine images for cell migration analysis using "File"→"Import"→"Image Sequence."
Check the box next to "Centroid" under "Analyze"→"Set Measurements."
Depict the edge of the selected cells in the first image.
